findings.issue_text: [BUG] poll_feed calls i.content.scrub on every feed item, but SimpleRSS only defines content for Atom feeds; for RSS 2.0 feeds (which have description, not content) i.content is nil and nil.scrub raises NoMethodError, aborting the entire poll run. Any site configuring feed_polling_url to an RSS 2.0 feed gets a crashed hourly job on every run; retry: false means the failure is silently dropped, and no topics are ever imported even though the feature is enabled.

[BUG] The Gemfile adds ruby-readability and simple-rss but the diff updates only Gemfile_rails4.lock; the primary Gemfile.lock is not regenerated, so the default bundle is out of sync with the Gemfile. A deploy running bundler with frozen/deployment mode (standard for production) fails with 'You are trying to install in deployment mode after changing your Gemfile' because Gemfile.lock lacks ruby-readability, simple-rss and guess_html_encoding; CI on the default lockfile also fails to boot once topic_retriever.rb is loaded, since the gem cannot be found.

[ADVISORY] The feed_key method (Redis-backed modified-time cache keyed on the feed URL) is defined but never called anywhere in the diff, so the feed is re-fetched and every item re-processed on each hourly run. Operators who enable feed polling get redundant full-feed fetches each hour; TopicEmbed.import's sha1 check masks most damage, but the dead method signals an unfinished 'only poll if modified' design that the next maintainer will either trip over or have to delete.

[ADVISORY] perform_retrieve invokes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inside the retrieve path, which re-parses and re-imports the entire feed on every cache-miss embed request rather than enqueueing the scheduled job. Each uncached embed/best request (up to one per URL per 60s) triggers a blocking full-feed download and import inside the sidekiq worker; a large feed means every retrieve_topic job is slow, and the return-value check only saves a second full pass.

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import marks imported posts as cook_method raw_html, which makes Post#cook return the raw remote HTML verbatim without any sanitization, and best.html.erb renders it with `raw post.cooked`. Any malicious HTML/JS in the polled RSS/Atom feed or the readability-extracted page becomes a stored XSS executed in the Discourse origin and in every embedding third-party page that includes the iframe; spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb only asserts post.cooked == post.raw, which enshrines the unsanitized behavior rather than verifying sanitization.

[BUG] The template closes the header conditional with `<%- end if %>` (line 6), which compiles to invalid Ruby `end if` with no condition, and no spec in the diff ever renders this view (spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb stubs TopicView and only checks success/headers), so the syntax error is never exercised. The first real request to /embed/best for an existing embed raises a SyntaxError/500 instead of rendering; every test passes because rendering is mocked out.

[BUG] poll_feed calls `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` with no nil check on i.content, and Atom/RSS feeds whose items carry only <summary>/<description> (no content) yield nil. The first feed item without a content element raises NoMethodError on nil.scrub; with sidekiq_options retry: false the whole hourly poll silently dies, so no feed items are ever imported and no operator-facing failure is recorded; spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only stubs the settings guards and never exercises poll_feed.

[BUG] poll_feed has no rescue around `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` or SimpleRSS.parse, and the job sets retry: false. A single transient DNS/timeout failure or a malformed feed body permanently kills that hour's poll with an unhandled exception and zero retries — feed import stops until the next scheduled run, with no verification or alerting that content was missed.

[ADVISORY] feed_key builds a `feed-modified:<sha1>` cache key but no code in the diff ever reads or writes it — the conditional-GET / modified-since verification it implies was silently dropped. Every hourly run re-downloads and re-parses the entire feed and re-enters TopicEmbed.import for every item; operators of large feeds pay full re-import cost each hour, and the dead method misleads the next maintainer into believing caching exists.

[BUG] When an existing TopicEmbed's post_id points to a deleted/missing post, `embed.post` is nil and `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises NoMethodError. A hard-deleted post (e.g., via a moderation cleanup that does not cascade to topic_embeds) makes every subsequent feed poll for that URL crash inside the job, and because update happens before embed.update_column, the embed row keeps pointing at the missing post forever with retry disabled.

[ADVISORY] The raw_html branch in Post#cook returns raw before reaching Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...), so embedded posts silently bypass the after_post_cook plugin filter that all regular posts pass through. Any plugin relying on after_post_cook (link rewrites, onebox injection, tracking) sees its behavior silently not applied to imported topics; the filter contract's requirement of applying to all cooked posts is dropped with no acceptance criterion covering it.

[ADVISORY] The loading view unconditionally reloads every 30 seconds with no retry cap and no terminal failure state, and retrieve_topic can permanently fail to create the embed (embeddable host mismatch, missing embed_by_username user, readability extraction failure). A visitor to a page whose retrieval fails gets an infinite 30-second reload loop inside the iframe, re-enqueueing retrieve_topic jobs and hammering the server indefinitely instead of seeing an error message; no spec covers the failed-retrieval path.

[ADVISORY] The `best` action builds TopicView.new(topic_id, ...) for whatever topic_id the topic_embeds row holds, with no handling for deleted topics or stale embed rows, and spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb mocks TopicView so the real lookup is never exercised. A topic deleted after its embed row was created makes /embed/best raise a RecordNotFound 500 inside the third-party iframe instead of a graceful fallback, leaving the embedding site with a broken comment box.

[ADVISORY] The referer check `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` rejects all requests from browsers that suppress the Referer header (rel="noreferrer", referrer-policy, privacy extensions), with no fallback verification. A subset of legitimate visitors on the embedding site — specifically any page using a referrer-suppressing policy — get a 403/404 error frame instead of comments, and the diff's spec asserts only the nil-referer rejection, never the legitimate-suppressed-referer user story.

[ADVISORY] The PR rewrites the Disqus import task and silently deletes the documented `-c/--category` CLI option, replacing the PostCreator path with TopicEmbed.import_remote. Operators running existing `disqus import -c <category>` scripts after this deploy get the option silently ignored (Thor raises for unknown option, breaking the script) and all imported topics land in the default category; this change is not traceable to any stated requirement of 'embed URL handling and validation'.

[BUG] An unrelated, pre-existing migration is modified to add `force: true` to create_table for top_topics. On any production database that has not yet run this migration (or on re-run), `force: true` drops the existing top_topics table and its data; this edit is unrelated to the embed feature and never should have been in the diff.

[BUG] poll_feed calls `i.content.scrub` unconditionally, but SimpleRSS exposes `content` only for Atom feeds; RSS 2.0 items expose `description` and `content` is nil, so `#scrub` raises NoMethodError. With feed_polling_enabled and an RSS (non-Atom) feed URL configured, the hourly job crashes on the first item after fetching, so no topics are ever imported and the failure is silent (retry: false discards the job).

[BUG] Post#cook returns `raw` verbatim for the raw_html cook method, bypassing the entire markdown/sanitization pipeline, and PostCreator accepts an arbitrary `cook_method` from @opts with no whitelist or permission check (lib/post_creator.rb:216). Any content scraped from the polled feed or the embeddable host is stored un-sanitized as cooked HTML and rendered with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view (and any other view of the topic), so a script tag in the RSS feed becomes stored XSS executed on every reader of the topic page; there is no invariant limiting raw_html to trusted imported content.

[ADVISORY] The embed client script is added as an asset-pipeline file with no route, admin page, or documented way for a third-party site to obtain and reference it (it relies on undefined globals discourseUrl/discourseEmbedUrl with no snippet generator anywhere in the diff). The embed feature ships inert: the site admin and the embedding site author have no supported way to get this script or set its required globals, so the feature cannot actually be used without hand-copying asset paths that include digest fingerprints.

[ADVISORY] The controller's referer check enforces only that the referer host equals embeddable_host, but does not validate that embed_url matches embeddable_host — a mismatched embed_url is passed to Jobs::RetrieveTopic and only filtered later by TopicRetriever#invalid_host?. The request-serving path enforces the host invariant in one place (TopicRetriever, whose invalid_host? check silently swallows mismatches) while the render path enforces it in a different place, so any future caller of TopicEmbed.import bypasses the embeddable_host restriction entirely; the controller's 1-minute-cached response is also served for arbitrary embed_url values before the retriever rejects them, sending unauthenticated clients 'loading' pages for URLs that will never be imported.

[ADVISORY] The new raw_html cook method returns `raw` completely unsanitized, so any HTML scraped from an external site (RSS feed content, readability-extracted pages, disqus imports) is stored and rendered verbatim with no HTML filtering. A malicious or compromised embedded site (or anyone controlling feed_polling_url content) gets stored XSS rendered on the Discourse origin in the embed view (`raw post.cooked` in best.html.erb), and any embed consumer's readers get script execution; the cook pipeline's sanitizer and plugin filters (after_post_cook is also skipped) are bypassed entirely for these posts.

[BUG] `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` validates the message origin with a substring containment test instead of exact origin equality. Any page whose origin string is a substring of discourseUrl (e.g. an attacker page at `http://discourseUrl.evil.com/` or any URL containing the discourse origin as a substring) passes the check and can drive `iframe.height` and, as the handler grows, other behavior — the height signal is attacker-controllable and the check is the only boundary in the embed client.

[BUG] The referer host check compares `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` as raw strings with no canonicalization on the setting side, while embed.js builds the request from a page on the admin-configured host. An admin who sets embeddable_host to `http://eviltrout.com`, `Eviltrout.com`, or `eviltrout.com/` (any form other than the exact bare lowercase host) makes every embed request fail with InvalidAccess — the X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL + best-posts endpoint is either unusable or the admin must guess the one canonical form; nothing normalizes the two sides.

[ADVISORY] `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."` assumes discourseUrl ends with a trailing slash, with no normalization. Publishers whose snippet sets discourseUrl without the trailing slash get a request to `http://forum.example.comembed/best` — a 404 and a silently broken embed with no error surfaced to them; the write side (publisher snippet) and read side (this concatenation) disagree on canonical form.

[BUG] To retrieve one embed URL, perform_retrieve synchronously executes the entire PollFeed job inline (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`), which re-parses the whole RSS/ATOM feed and re-runs TopicEmbed.import for every feed item. A single embed request for an article not in the feed still triggers a full feed fetch plus N import lookups on the Sidekiq worker; with a large feed this blocks the worker for the whole parse and hammers the publisher's feed server on every embed miss (throttled only per-URL, once per 60s per URL, not per feed) — an unbounded N-for-1 work amplification on the retrieve path.

[ADVISORY] `feed_key` computes a Redis key from the feed URL but no code in the diff ever reads or writes that key. Dead/phantom derived data: a reader (or the next maintainer implementing conditional polling) will assume the modified-since throttle exists when nothing is stored — the hourly job unconditionally re-fetches and re-processes every feed item forever; the helper implies caching behavior the code does not implement.

[ADVISORY] `rss.items.each` iterates the entire feed with no item cap, no since-marker, and `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no timeout — and it runs on an hourly schedule with retry: false. A large or slow/hung feed stalls the scheduled job worker indefinitely (no open timeout) and materializes all items in memory every hour even when nothing changed; a single hung fetch blocks all other sidetiq-scheduled jobs sharing that worker.

[ADVISORY] When no topic exists yet the action enqueues RetrieveTopic and renders a 'loading' page whose only retry mechanism is `setTimeout(reload, 30000)`. Every first-time embed visitor's browser polls the full endpoint once per 30 seconds indefinitely — the dimensioned magic number 30000 is unexplained and unconfigurable, and a permanently failing retrieval (invalid host, feed not containing the URL, embed_by_username unset) leaves the visitor in an infinite reload loop with no error surface.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import has a check-then-insert race: it SELECTs for the embed, then creates the TopicEmbed inside a transaction, with no rescue around the unique-index violation and no upsert. Two concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs for the same new embed_url (the 60s Redis throttle is best-effort setnx, and staff bypass it via no_throttle) both pass the `embed.blank?` check and both create topics; the loser's TopicEmbed.create! raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, but its PostCreator-created topic was already committed in the same outer transaction path depending on nesting — leaving duplicate topics or a failed job depending on transaction boundaries.

[ADVISORY] import_remote calls `open(url).read` with no timeout, size limit, or content-type check before feeding the result to Readability. The RetrieveTopic worker (triggerable by any visitor to an embedded page once per URL per 60s, and unlimited for staff no_throttle) can be held indefinitely by a slow target host, tying up Sidekiq workers — a cheap external denial-of-worker vector when embeddable_host points at a third-party site the Discourse operator does not control.

[ADVISORY] The resize postMessage uses `'<%= request.referer %>'` as targetOrigin, but the embed is loaded inside an iframe whose `request.referer` may be empty or differ from the embedding page in some browser/referrer-policy configurations. When referer is empty, `parent.postMessage(..., '')` throws a SyntaxError and the resize never fires, leaving the iframe at its default height with clipped comments — a format drift between what the controller validated and what the layout echoes back as the trusted target origin.

[ADVISORY] absolutize_urls only rewrites hrefs/srcs that start with a literal '/', so protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.example.com/img.png`) and relative paths without leading slash (`img/wat.jpg`) pass through unresolved. Feed-imported posts whose images use the common `//` protocol-relative form render broken image links in the embedded comments — the relative-URL normalization the comment claims ('Convert any relative URLs to absolute') is not what the code implements.

[BUG] The `-c/--category` import option was silently removed and all imported topics now go to the default category regardless of the operator's choice. An operator running the documented `thor disqus:import -c News -p admin` gets a deprecation/unknown-option error (or, if thor ignores unknown options, every imported topic lands in uncategorized), silently changing the import objective with no human acceptance of the behavior change.

[BUG] The new raw_html cook_method short-circuits before Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook), so the established plugin contract that every cooked post passes through after_post_cook filters is broken for imported posts. Any site with a plugin hooking after_post_cook (e.g. to sanitize, transform links, or add attribution) sees its filter silently skipped on every RSS-imported post; plugins degrade without any error, and the skip is invisible because the post still 'cooks'.

[ADVISORY] RSS/embed content is stored as cooked HTML via cook_method raw_html with skip_validations: true and no sanitization step, bypassing the normal markdown pipeline that guarantees cooked post HTML is safe. A malicious or compromised feed (or a compromised embeddable_host page fetched by readability) injects arbitrary HTML/script into post.cooked, which the embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, executing in visitors' browsers on the Discourse domain — an operator enabling feed polling on an untrusted feed gets stored XSS with no warning.

[ADVISORY] The postMessage origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring match, so an origin like `http://forum.example.com.attacker.com` passes when discourseUrl is `http://forum.example.com`. Any attacker who embeds a page whose origin contains the forum URL as a substring can drive `discourse-resize` messages at the iframe; the damage is limited to height manipulation (and a string e.data from legacy browsers is silently ignored), so it is a hardening gap rather than a data-loss path.

[ADVISORY] The resize postMessage uses `request.referer` as targetOrigin, which is the full URL including path and query rather than an origin, and is the client-supplied referer rather than a validated value. Per spec a non-matching targetOrigin causes the message to be silently dropped, so when the referer's full string does not exactly equal the parent window's origin the iframe never resizes and the embed renders clipped; this fails intermittently depending on the embedding page's URL shape.

[ADVISORY] perform_retrieve synchronously executes the entire PollFeed job (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`) inline, which parses and imports the whole feed inside a single background job step. A single embed miss for one article triggers a full-feed poll, re-importing every feed item within that job's runtime and retry budget; a large or slow feed makes the RetrieveTopic job long-running and retries on feed fetch failure reduplicate work that the hourly scheduler already owns — duplicate sources of truth for when the feed is polled.

[BUG] cook_method raw_html returns the raw input verbatim, so un-sanitized HTML fetched from remote feeds/pages is stored as cooked content and rendered with `raw post.cooked` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:20, enabling stored XSS. Any HTML/JavaScript in the RSS feed (SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) or in the readability-extracted page content — including content injected by a compromised embeddable_host or feed source — is stored verbatim and executed in the browser of every visitor who loads /embed/best, stealing session credentials and performing actions as that user.

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import interpolates the URL into raw HTML without escaping: `"...#{url}"`, and the guard `url =~ /^https?:\/\//` only checks the scheme prefix, so the rest of the URL can contain single quotes and HTML. A feed item link or remote page URL like `http://x/' onmouseover='alert(1)` or `http://x/'>

[BUG] The client-controlled Referer header is interpolated unescaped into a JavaScript string literal: `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. An attacker requests /embed/best directly with a Referer whose host matches embeddable_host but whose body contains quote/paren characters (e.g. `http://eviltrout.com/x');alert(document.cookie);//`), which still passes the URI(referer).host check in ensure_embeddable, yielding reflected XSS in the embed page served from the Discourse origin.

[ADVISORY] PollFeed calls Kernel#open on a config-backed URL: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`, and Ruby's open-uri Kernel#open executes shell commands when the string begins with a pipe character. The feed_polling_url site setting is fetched as-is; any value starting with `|` (set by a compromised admin account or a staff member with settings access, since this setting is not restricted to admins-only) causes arbitrary command execution on the Discourse server, hourly, with sidekiq's privileges.

[ADVISORY] The only authorization gate for the embeddable content is a client-supplied Referer header (`URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), which is trivially spoofable and absent for direct GETs from curl/browsers that suppress Referer. Anyone can curl /embed/best?embed_url=... with a forged Referer matching the configured host to read topic content (best posts) of any topic that has a TopicEmbed row, regardless of the topic's category read-restrictions as enforced elsewhere in Discourse's normal topic access flow — private/limited-category content leaks to unauthenticated scrapers.

[ADVISORY] The postMessage origin check uses substring matching (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`) instead of exact origin equality, so any origin that is a substring of the configured discourseUrl passes (e.g. `http:` matching, or an origin appearing anywhere inside the URL string). A malicious page on any host whose origin string appears within the discourseUrl value can send accepted `discourse-resize` messages; impact is limited to controlling the iframe height (layout manipulation/phishing overlay), but the check is structurally unsound and will be copy-pasted for future message handlers with real authority.

[ADVISORY] invalid_host? compares SiteSetting.embeddable_host to URI(@embed_url).host without case normalization or port/scheme pinning, and the throttle key `"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"` is un-normalized. Non-admin requesters can trigger server-side fetches (TopicEmbed.import_remote → open(url)) of the embeddable host at will by varying trivial URL spellings (trailing dots, case, fragments), defeating the 60-second redis throttle; combined with Jobs.enqueue in EmbedController#best this gives an unauthenticated user a cheap lever for server-side request floods against the configured host.

[ADVISORY] The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' tests pass because of the unstubbed feed_polling_enabled? default (false), not because of the condition each test names. A regression that breaks the url/username guards in poll_feed.rb:12-13 still passes these specs, since poll_feed is never called in either test regardless of the named setting — the tests give false confidence that the guard logic is verified.

[ADVISORY] The entire poll_feed body (feed fetching, SimpleRSS parsing, link/id selection, CGI.unescapeHTML, TopicEmbed.import loop) has zero test coverage — the only passing-path test stubs poll_feed itself. Any crash or logic error in app/jobs/poll_feed.rb:18-38 (e.g. i.content returning nil, an item whose link is neither http nor https, an unparsable feed) is invisible to the suite; checked spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb, and spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb — no test exercises the parsing path.

[ADVISORY] Both 'valid host' branch tests stub retrieved_recently?, so the real Redis throttle logic in topic_retriever.rb:29-37 (setnx/expire, the 60-second window) is never executed by any test. A regression in the throttle (e.g. the setnx/expire race or key format change) passes the suite because the tests only verify that a mocked predicate routes to a mocked perform_retrieve — the actual gatekeeping behavior is untested.

[ADVISORY] The 'Supports updating the post' test only asserts the new content appears in cooked; it never asserts content_sha1 was updated, and the skip-revision branch (content_sha1 unchanged) has no test at all. If TopicEmbed.import's change-detection guard (topic_embed.rb:31) breaks — double-revising every poll or never updating content_sha1 so every import re-revises — the spec still passes, so the most bug-prone branch of the update path (digest comparison) ships with no verification.

[ADVISORY] The 'tells the topic retriever to work' test mocks TopicRetriever.new/ retrieve directly, but the controller under test calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) — the assertion verifies the retriever mock, never that the job was enqueued with the correct user_id and embed_url arguments. If the controller enqueues the job with wrong or missing arguments (e.g. a nil embed_url or a renamed job), this test still passes whenever the test harness runs jobs inline — the actual producer-side contract (controller → retrieve_topic job args) is unverified.

[BUG] An already-shipped migration is modified to add force: true, making it destructive on re-run. Any environment that re-runs this migration (db:migrate:redo, a restored database whose schema_migrations lost the row, or a partial-migration recovery) has top_topics silently dropped and rebuilt empty, losing all computed top-topic metrics data with no backup step.

[ADVISORY] The topic_embeds table declares null: false topic_id/post_id integer columns with no foreign keys and no non-unique indexes on either column. When a topic or post is later deleted (staff delete, or TopicDestroyer), the corresponding topic_embed row is left dangling with no FK/cascade to clean it; EmbedController#best then calls TopicView.new on a deleted topic_id and errors, and TopicEmbed.import's update path calls PostRevisor.new(embed.post).revise! with a nil post and crashes with NoMethodError — operators get a 500 on the embed endpoint until rows are manually purged.

[BUG] poll_feed calls CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), which raises NoMethodError on any RSS 2.0 feed item that lacks a content element (SimpleRSS maps description for RSS, content only for Atom, and i.content is nil for plain RSS feeds). The hourly PollFeed job crashes mid-run with retry: false, so no feed items are ever imported and previously-processed items earlier in the loop have already had topics created while the remainder of the feed is silently never imported; the same feed_url then fails on every subsequent poll.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import creates topics with skip_validations: true and no title presence check, so a feed item with a blank/missing title produces a topic with an empty title and an empty-title post. RSS feeds with items lacking titles silently create broken topics on the forum (no title, only the auto-appended 'imported from' footer), which then appear in topic lists and the embed endpoint's 'start_discussion' view; the data is junk at creation time and cannot be trivially repaired since the source feed has no title.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import interpolates the feed-provided url into the HTML footer string with #{url} inside a double-quoted Ruby string rather than through Nokogiri/parameterized construction. Beyond the injection angle (Security's), the data-integrity failure is that a feed link containing an unescaped ampersand or quote is emitted as malformed HTML into the post raw, which (combined with cook_method raw_html bypassing the cooking/sanitization pipeline) is permanently stored as-is and re-served verbatim on every embed render.

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url) with no timeout and no size cap on a job triggered by a user-facing embed request. A slow or hanging source server makes the retrieve_topic sidekiq worker block indefinitely on the socket read, exhausting sidekiq workers; a huge page is read fully into memory. The embed page meanwhile reloads every 30 seconds forever showing 'Loading Discussion'.

[BUG] poll_feed calls SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) with no timeout, and the job sets sidekiq_options retry: false. A hanging or slow feed URL blocks the scheduled job indefinitely; when open raises (DNS failure, 404, malformed feed), the exception is raised in a job with retries disabled and no logging call anywhere in the diff, so feed import silently stops forever with zero operator-visible signal.

[BUG] In the update path, embed.post is used without a nil check; if the post has been deleted (or post_id dangles), PostRevisor.new(nil) raises NoMethodError. PollFeed or retrieve_topic crashes with NoMethodError on nil post inside the scheduled/retry:false job, aborting the whole remaining feed items for that run, and the embed page for that URL keeps showing the loading view indefinitely because no embed state ever changes.

[BUG] On the update path, embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...) runs unconditionally after revisor.revise!, even when the underlying @post.save fails its validations, so the hash is advanced while the write failed. A failed post revision is recorded as done: on every subsequent poll the content_sha1 comparison shows 'no change' and the revision is never re-attempted, so the post silently stays stale forever while the pipeline reports success.

[BUG] When PostCreator.create returns a failed (invalid) post, the transaction commits with no TopicEmbed row created and no error raised; import returns nil silently. The retrieve_topic job completes 'successfully' while dropping the work; the user's embed iframe reloads the loading page every 30 seconds in an infinite loop with no error surfaced anywhere, because the controller will re-enqueue retrieve_topic each time and the throttle only hides it for 60s.

[BUG] retrieved_recently? commits the Redis throttle key (setnx + expire) before perform_retrieve runs, so a failed retrieve still consumes the 60-second slot. When the fetch or import fails (bad page, readability returns empty content, nil user), subsequent embed requests within 60 seconds no-op 'successfully' against the throttle, and combined with the silent nil return of fetch_http the embedding site shows the loading page indefinitely with no diagnostic.

[BUG] fetch_http silently returns when the embed_by_username user is missing or embed_by_username is unset, with no error surfaced. A site that enables embedding but leaves embed_by_username blank gets a permanently broken embed flow: every request enqueues retrieve_topic which silently does nothing, and the loading page reloads every 30 seconds forever; nothing in the UI or logs tells the operator the setting is the cause.

[BUG] When a topic_id is found but the topic no longer exists (deleted/removed), TopicView.new raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound, producing a raw 500 on the public embed/best endpoint. A dangling TopicEmbed row (topic soft-deleted or hard-removed) turns every embed view for that URL into a server error with no recovery path — the controller never falls back to re-enqueueing retrieve_topic or rendering loading.

[BUG] CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) raises NoMethodError when an RSS item has no content element (i.content is nil), aborting the items loop mid-iteration. One malformed item in the feed stops all subsequent feed items from being imported on every hourly run (retry: false), so the feed silently stops importing new entries with no log or error report.

[ADVISORY] feed_key (the Redis key 'feed-modified:...') is defined but never read or written anywhere in the diff — the conditional fetch it was evidently built for is unimplemented. Every hourly run re-fetches and re-processes the full feed even when nothing changed, and TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve also invokes a full synchronous poll_feed on each cold embed view; large feeds multiply the outbound fetch and PostRevisor work per request with no modified-since check to short-circuit it.

[ADVISORY] perform_retrieve runs Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inside the retrieve_topic worker on the embed request path. Every first-time embed view of any URL on the embeddable host triggers a full RSS/ATOM download, parse, and potential import of every feed item — one user viewing a blog post can cause dozens of topic creations, and a slow feed server delays the embed response path's worker for the full poll duration.

[ADVISORY] The loading view unconditionally reloads itself every 30 seconds with no retry cap or error state, combined with the retrieve flow having no failure signal back to the iframe. When retrieve_topic fails silently (nil user, failed PostCreator, throttled retry, unreachable source), the embedding site's readers get a permanently 'Loading Discussion...' iframe that hammers the Discourse embed/best endpoint every 30 seconds per visitor, indefinitely.

The diff doesn’t establish that the hook must run for raw_html posts, so it’s not a provable defect, but it is a concrete behavior/compatibility concern introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The loading view unconditionally reloads every 30 seconds with no retry cap and no terminal failure state, and retrieve_topic can permanently fail to create the embed (embeddable host mismatch, missing embed_by_username user, readability extraction failure). While `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` throttles the actual fetch, it does not prevent repeated job creation/execution, so the diff introduces a real broken/failure behavior for end users and avoidable server load.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `best` action builds TopicView.new(topic_id, ...) for whatever topic_id the topic_embeds row holds, with no handling for deleted topics or stale embed rows, and spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb mocks TopicView so the real lookup is never exercised. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new raw_html cook method returns `raw` completely unsanitized, so any HTML scraped from an external site (RSS feed content, readability-extracted pages, disqus imports) is stored and rendered verbatim with no HTML filtering. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The referer host check compares `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` as raw strings with no canonicalization on the setting side, while embed.js builds the request from a page on the admin-configured host. If an admin enters a value including a scheme (`http://eviltrout.com`), a trailing slash (`eviltrout.com/`), or different casing, the string comparison will fail and raise `Discourse::InvalidAccess`, breaking embedding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] To retrieve one embed URL, perform_retrieve synchronously executes the entire PollFeed job inline (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`), which re-parses the whole RSS/ATOM feed and re-runs TopicEmbed.import for every feed item. This is a real, diff-grounded performance/scalability/architecture concern, but it’s not a direct correctness defect (the code still functions as designed).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `feed_key` computes a Redis key from the feed URL but no code in the diff ever reads or writes that key. Dead/phantom derived data: a reader (or the next maintainer implementing conditional polling) will assume the modified-since throttle exists when nothing is stored — the hourly job unconditionally re-fetches and re-processes every feed item forever; the helper implies caching behavior the code does not implement.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined to derive a Redis key from `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`, but no code in the diff ever uses `feed_key` (no `$redis.get/set`, no conditional fetch headers, etc.). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `rss.items.each` iterates the entire feed with no item cap, no since-marker, and `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no timeout — and it runs on an hourly schedule with retry: false. This is a real reliability/performance defect introduced by the diff, especially since `sidekiq_options retry: false` means it won’t recover via retries if it errors but can still hang on I/O.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When no topic exists yet the action enqueues RetrieveTopic and renders a 'loading' page whose only retry mechanism is `setTimeout(reload, 30000)`. Every first-time embed visitor's browser polls the full endpoint once per 30 seconds indefinitely — the dimensioned magic number 30000 is unexplained and unconfigurable, and a permanently failing retrieval (invalid host, feed not containing the URL, embed_by_username unset) leaves the visitor in an infinite reload loop with no error surface.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` whose only behavior is `setTimeout(function(){ document.location.reload(); }, 30000);`, and `EmbedController#best` renders this template whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil (after enqueuing `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`). There is no termination condition or error surface in the loading view, and the 30000ms retry is a hardcoded magic number. If retrieval never results in a `TopicEmbed` (e.g., fetch fails or settings prevent creation), the client will keep reloading/polling indefinitely. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import has a check-then-insert race: it SELECTs for the embed, then creates the TopicEmbed inside a transaction, with no rescue around the unique-index violation and no upsert. Two concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs for the same new embed_url (the 60s Redis throttle is best-effort setnx, and staff bypass it via no_throttle) both pass the `embed.blank?` check and both create topics; the loser's TopicEmbed.create! raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, but its PostCreator-created topic was already committed in the same outer transaction path depending on nesting — leaving duplicate topics or a failed job depending on transaction boundaries.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the code does a non-atomic check-then-create: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` followed by `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` inside `Topic.transaction` when `embed.blank?`. With the unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, two concurrent imports of the same new URL can both see no row and attempt `create!`; the loser will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and the job will fail (no rescue/upsert present in the diff). The Redis throttle in TopicRetriever is explicitly bypassable via `no_throttle` (staff) and is best-effort, so concurrent RetrieveTopic executions are plausible per the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] import_remote calls `open(url).read` with no timeout, size limit, or content-type check before feeding the result to Readability. The RetrieveTopic worker (triggerable by any visitor to an embedded page once per URL per 60s, and unlimited for staff no_throttle) can be held indefinitely by a slow target host, tying up Sidekiq workers — a cheap external denial-of-worker vector when embeddable_host points at a third-party site the Discourse operator does not control.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote` which does `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) without any explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`, response size limit, or content-type validation. This method is invoked from `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` (lib/topic_retriever.rb), which is executed by the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` Sidekiq job (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb) enqueued by `EmbedController#best` when an embed is missing (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). Because the job performs a network fetch synchronously inside the worker, a slow/hanging remote host can tie up Sidekiq worker threads/processes. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The resize postMessage uses `'<%= request.referer %>'` as targetOrigin, but the embed is loaded inside an iframe whose `request.referer` may be empty or differ from the embedding page in some browser/referrer-policy configurations. adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, the code calls `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. `postMessage`’s `targetOrigin` must be an origin (scheme+host+port) or `*`, not a full referrer URL with a path/query. Since `request.referer` will typically be a full URL (e.g. `https://site.com/page`), this can raise a `SyntaxError/DOMException` and prevent the resize message from being sent, breaking iframe sizing. The finding’s “referer may be empty” part is less supported because `ensure_embeddable` rejects missing referrers, but the invalid `targetOrigin` issue is directly grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] absolutize_urls only rewrites hrefs/srcs that start with a literal '/', so protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.example.com/img.png`) and relative paths without leading slash (`img/wat.jpg`) pass through unresolved. Feed-imported posts whose images use the common `//` protocol-relative form render broken image links in the embedded comments — the relative-URL normalization the comment claims ('Convert any relative URLs to absolute') is not what the code implements.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, only `href`/`src` values where `start_with?('/')` are rewritten. That means relative paths like `img/wat.jpg` are left unchanged despite the comment claiming “Convert any relative URLs to absolute.” Also, protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png` *do* match `start_with?('/')` and will be rewritten to `#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/img.png` (because of `sub(/^\/+/, '')`), which is incorrect and can break external asset links. This is a real correctness issue in the diff-grounded URL normalization logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The `-c/--category` import option was silently removed and all imported topics now go to the default category regardless of the operator's choice. An operator running the documented `thor disqus:import -c News -p admin` gets a deprecation/unknown-option error (or, if thor ignores unknown options, every imported topic lands in uncategorized), silently changing the import objective with no human acceptance of the behavior change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the Disqus Thor task’s `:category` option (`method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` deleted) and deletes the logic that looked up `category_id` and passed it into `PostCreator` (`category: category_id`). The new implementation calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)` with no category parameter, so operators can no longer specify `-c/--category`; running the previously supported command would now raise an unknown-option error and, even if adapted, imports would no longer be routed to a chosen category via this task.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new raw_html cook_method short-circuits before Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook), so the established plugin contract that every cooked post passes through after_post_cook filters is broken for imported posts. Any site with a plugin hooking after_post_cook (e.g. to sanitize, transform links, or add attribution) sees its filter silently skipped on every RSS-imported post; plugins degrade without any error, and the skip is invisible because the post still 'cooks'.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook now returns `raw` immediately when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses the existing `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` call. That means any plugins relying on the `after_post_cook` hook will not run for these raw_html (e.g. RSS-imported) posts, a behavioral regression introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] RSS/embed content is stored as cooked HTML via cook_method raw_html with skip_validations: true and no sanitization step, bypassing the normal markdown pipeline that guarantees cooked post HTML is safe. A malicious or compromised feed (or a compromised embeddable_host page fetched by readability) injects arbitrary HTML/script into post.cooked, which the embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, executing in visitors' browsers on the Discourse domain — an operator enabling feed polling on an untrusted feed gets stored XSS with no warning.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a raw HTML cooking path: `Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb), and TopicEmbed imports set `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` with `skip_validations: true` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postMessage origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring match, so an origin like `http://forum.example.com.attacker.com` passes when discourseUrl is `http://forum.example.com`. Any attacker who embeds a page whose origin contains the forum URL as a substring can drive `discourse-resize` messages at the iframe; the damage is limited to height manipulation (and a string e.data from legacy browsers is silently ignored), so it is a hardening gap rather than a data-loss path.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the check is `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, i.e., it only accepts messages when `e.origin` is a substring of `discourseUrl`. For the scenario described (`discourseUrl = http://forum.example.com`, `e.origin = http://forum.example.com.attacker.com`), `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` would be `-1` (because `e.origin` is longer), so the message is rejected. The finding reverses the substring relationship and therefore does not match the diff’s behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The resize postMessage uses `request.referer` as targetOrigin, which is the full URL including path and query rather than an origin, and is the client-supplied referer rather than a validated value. Per spec a non-matching targetOrigin causes the message to be silently dropped, so when the referer's full string does not exactly equal the parent window's origin the iframe never resizes and the embed renders clipped; this fails intermittently depending on the embedding page's URL shape.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `postMessage` is using `request.referer` as `targetOrigin`, which is a full URL (path/query) rather than the required origin (scheme+host+port), and notes this causes non-matching targetOrigin and silent message drops leading to failed resizing—same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] perform_retrieve synchronously executes the entire PollFeed job (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`) inline, which parses and imports the whole feed inside a single background job step. A single embed miss for one article triggers a full-feed poll, re-importing every feed item within that job's runtime and retry budget; a large or slow feed makes the RetrieveTopic job long-running and retries on feed fetch failure reduplicate work that the hourly scheduler already owns — duplicate sources of truth for when the feed is polled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] cook_method raw_html returns the raw input verbatim, so un-sanitized HTML fetched from remote feeds/pages is stored as cooked content and rendered with `raw post.cooked` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:20, enabling stored XSS. Any HTML/JavaScript in the RSS feed (SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) or in the readability-extracted page content — including content injected by a compromised embeddable_host or feed source — is stored verbatim and executed in the browser of every visitor who loads /embed/best, stealing session credentials and performing actions as that user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed.import interpolates the URL into raw HTML without escaping: `"...#{url}"`, and the guard `url =~ /^https?:\/\//` only checks the scheme prefix, so the rest of the URL can contain single quotes and HTML. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] PollFeed calls Kernel#open on a config-backed URL: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`, and Ruby's open-uri Kernel#open executes shell commands when the string begins with a pipe character. The feed_polling_url site setting is fetched as-is; any value starting with `|` (set by a compromised admin account or a staff member with settings access, since this setting is not restricted to admins-only) causes arbitrary command execution on the Discourse server, hourly, with sidekiq's privileges.

Ruby's `Kernel#open` supports the `|cmd` form (popen) when given a string beginning with `|`, so passing a site-setting-backed string into `open` can allow command execution if that setting is set to such a value. The diff shows the setting is used as-is with no validation/sanitization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only authorization gate for the embeddable content is a client-supplied Referer header (`URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), which is trivially spoofable and absent for direct GETs from curl/browsers that suppress Referer. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postMessage origin check uses substring matching (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`) instead of exact origin equality, so any origin that is a substring of the configured discourseUrl passes (e.g. `http:` matching, or an origin appearing anywhere inside the URL string). A malicious page on any host whose origin string appears within the discourseUrl value can send accepted `discourse-resize` messages; impact is limited to controlling the iframe height (layout manipulation/phishing overlay), but the check is structurally unsound and will be copy-pasted for future message handlers with real authority.

adjudication.rationale: In newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, `postMessageReceived` validates the sender with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This is substring matching against `discourseUrl` (which is a full URL string), not an exact origin comparison. As a result, an attacker-controlled origin that appears as a substring within `discourseUrl` could bypass the check and send `discourse-resize` messages that will be accepted and used to set `iframe.height`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] invalid_host? compares SiteSetting.embeddable_host to URI(@embed_url).host without case normalization or port/scheme pinning, and the throttle key `"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"` is un-normalized. Non-admin requesters can trigger server-side fetches (TopicEmbed.import_remote → open(url)) of the embeddable host at will by varying trivial URL spellings (trailing dots, case, fragments), defeating the 60-second redis throttle; combined with Jobs.enqueue in EmbedController#best this gives an unauthenticated user a cheap lever for server-side request floods against the configured host.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, `invalid_host?` only checks `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host` with no normalization (case, trailing dot) and no port/scheme constraints, and `retrieved_recently?` uses a Redis key of `"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"`, so trivial URL variations (e.g., fragment/query/case/port) produce different keys and bypass the 60s throttle. In `EmbedController#best`, when no existing embed is found it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)` and the action is not authenticated (only referer-host checked), so repeated requests can trigger repeated server-side `open(url)` fetch attempts via `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, enabling request flooding against the configured host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' tests pass because of the unstubbed feed_polling_enabled? default (false), not because of the condition each test names. A regression that breaks the url/username guards in poll_feed.rb:12-13 still passes these specs, since poll_feed is never called in either test regardless of the named setting — the tests give false confidence that the guard logic is verified.

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute the guard is a conjunction: `feed_polling_enabled? && feed_polling_url.present? && embed_by_username.present?` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:14-16). In the specs, the tests named “requires feed_polling_url” and “requires embed_by_username” only stub the one setting under test (to nil) and do not stub `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` to true. Given the default in config/site_settings.yml sets `feed_polling_enabled: false`, the guard fails on the first condition, so `poll_feed` is never called regardless of URL/username presence—meaning those two specs don’t actually verify the intended guards and could miss regressions to the url/username checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The entire poll_feed body (feed fetching, SimpleRSS parsing, link/id selection, CGI.unescapeHTML, TopicEmbed.import loop) has zero test coverage — the only passing-path test stubs poll_feed itself. Any crash or logic error in app/jobs/poll_feed.rb:18-38 (e.g. i.content returning nil, an item whose link is neither http nor https, an unparsable feed) is invisible to the suite; checked spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb, and spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb — no test exercises the parsing path.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` introduces nontrivial logic in `poll_feed` (fetch via `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`, `SimpleRSS.parse`, iterating `rss.items`, `i.link`/`i.id` fallback, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and `TopicEmbed.import(...)`). The added spec `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only verifies gating in `execute` and, on the success path, stubs/expect-calls `poll_feed` without exercising its body. Other added specs (`spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`) do not cover the feed parsing/fetch loop either. So crashes/edge cases inside `poll_feed` would indeed be untested based on what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Both 'valid host' branch tests stub retrieved_recently?, so the real Redis throttle logic in topic_retriever.rb:29-37 (setnx/expire, the 60-second window) is never executed by any test. A regression in the throttle (e.g. the setnx/expire race or key format change) passes the suite because the tests only verify that a mocked predicate routes to a mocked perform_retrieve — the actual gatekeeping behavior is untested.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, both “with a valid host” examples stub `retrieved_recently?` (`returns(false)` / `returns(true)`) and only assert whether `perform_retrieve` is invoked. This means the real Redis throttle implementation in lib/topic_retriever.rb (`$redis.setnx`, `$redis.expire`, 60-second window, and key format `retrieved:#{@embed_url}`) is not exercised by any test, so regressions in that gatekeeping logic could slip through.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'Supports updating the post' test only asserts the new content appears in cooked; it never asserts content_sha1 was updated, and the skip-revision branch (content_sha1 unchanged) has no test at all. If TopicEmbed.import's change-detection guard (topic_embed.rb:31) breaks — double-revising every poll or never updating content_sha1 so every import re-revises — the spec still passes, so the most bug-prone branch of the update path (digest comparison) ships with no verification.

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds change-detection logic in TopicEmbed.import: it computes content_sha1 and only revises the existing post when `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`, then persists the new digest via `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb, update branch). The new spec "Supports updating the post" only asserts `post.cooked` contains new contents after a second import (spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb) and does not assert that `content_sha1` was updated, nor does it test the guard path where the digest is unchanged (i.e., no revision should occur). This is a concrete, diff-grounded missing-test-coverage concern for the most error-prone branch, but not a verifiable runtime defect in the implementation itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'tells the topic retriever to work' test mocks TopicRetriever.new/ retrieve directly, but the controller under test calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) — the assertion verifies the retriever mock, never that the job was enqueued with the correct user_id and embed_url arguments. If the controller enqueues the job with wrong or missing arguments (e.g. a nil embed_url or a renamed job), this test still passes whenever the test harness runs jobs inline — the actual producer-side contract (controller → retrieve_topic job args) is unverified.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` is found it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`; it does not directly instantiate `TopicRetriever`. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`'s "tells the topic retriever to work" example mocks `TopicRetriever.new` and `retriever.retrieve`, so it is not directly verifying the producer-side contract that the controller enqueues the `:retrieve_topic` job with the correct arguments. This is a test coverage/accuracy issue rather than an application behavior defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] An already-shipped migration is modified to add force: true, making it destructive on re-run. Any environment that re-runs this migration (db:migrate:redo, a restored database whose schema_migrations lost the row, or a partial-migration recovery) has top_topics silently dropped and rebuilt empty, losing all computed top-topic metrics data with no backup step.

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` to use `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it, so re-running this migration (e.g., `db:migrate:redo` or any scenario where the migration is executed again) can silently destroy existing `top_topics` data with no backup/migration step shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The topic_embeds table declares null: false topic_id/post_id integer columns with no foreign keys and no non-unique indexes on either column. When a topic or post is later deleted (staff delete, or TopicDestroyer), the corresponding topic_embed row is left dangling with no FK/cascade to clean it; EmbedController#best then calls TopicView.new on a deleted topic_id and errors, and TopicEmbed.import's update path calls PostRevisor.new(embed.post).revise! with a nil post and crashes with NoMethodError — operators get a 500 on the embed endpoint until rows are manually purged.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `topic_embeds` with required `topic_id`/`post_id` (migration `CreateTopicEmbeds`) but no foreign keys/cascades and `TopicEmbed` has no `dependent: :destroy` hooks. The new code then assumes referential integrity: `EmbedController#best` uses `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` and unconditionally does `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` if it returns an id, and `TopicEmbed.import`’s update path does `post = embed.post` and immediately `PostRevisor.new(post)` without guarding `post.nil?`. If a topic or post is deleted while its `topic_embeds` row remains, these call sites can raise (nil post / missing topic), producing 500s as described. This dangling-row scenario is enabled by what the diff adds and is not mitigated in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] poll_feed calls CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), which raises NoMethodError on any RSS 2.0 feed item that lacks a content element (SimpleRSS maps description for RSS, content only for Atom, and i.content is nil for plain RSS feeds). The hourly PollFeed job crashes mid-run with retry: false, so no feed items are ever imported and previously-processed items earlier in the loop have already had topics created while the remainder of the feed is silently never imported; the same feed_url then fails on every subsequent poll.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the code unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If `i.content` is `nil` for some feed items, this will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil.scrub`, aborting the job mid-loop. The job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so failures won’t be retried, and the remaining items won’t be imported once the exception occurs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import creates topics with skip_validations: true and no title presence check, so a feed item with a blank/missing title produces a topic with an empty title and an empty-title post. RSS feeds with items lacking titles silently create broken topics on the forum (no title, only the auto-appended 'imported from' footer), which then appear in topic lists and the embed endpoint's 'start_discussion' view; the data is junk at creation time and cannot be trivially repaired since the source feed has no title.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, new topics/posts are created via `PostCreator.new(... title: title, ... skip_validations: true ...)` with no guard that `title` is present/nonblank (app/models/topic_embed.rb). Feed polling passes `i.title` directly (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), and RSS/Atom items can have missing/blank titles. Because validations are explicitly skipped, the diff shows a clear path to persisting a topic/post with an empty title, producing low-quality/broken data at creation time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import interpolates the feed-provided url into the HTML footer string with #{url} inside a double-quoted Ruby string rather than through Nokogiri/parameterized construction. Beyond the injection angle (Security's), the data-integrity failure is that a feed link containing an unescaped ampersand or quote is emitted as malformed HTML into the post raw, which (combined with cook_method raw_html bypassing the cooking/sanitization pipeline) is permanently stored as-is and re-served verbatim on every embed render.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the footer is built via string interpolation: `"#{url}"` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). Although `url` is checked to start with `http(s)://`, it is not HTML-escaped, so URLs containing characters like `&`, `'`, or `"` can produce malformed HTML (e.g., break the `href` attribute). This is compounded by `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returning `raw` verbatim for `:raw_html`, permanently storing and re-serving the unescaped HTML without the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url) with no timeout and no size cap on a job triggered by a user-facing embed request. A slow or hanging source server makes the retrieve_topic sidekiq worker block indefinitely on the socket read, exhausting sidekiq workers; a huge page is read fully into memory. The embed page meanwhile reloads every 30 seconds forever showing 'Loading Discussion'.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote` which does `open(url).read` (lib/topic_embed.rb) with no timeout or size limit. This method is called from `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, which is invoked by `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb). That job is enqueued directly from the user-facing `EmbedController#best` when no embed exists (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). A slow/hanging remote server can therefore block a Sidekiq worker indefinitely and a very large response will be fully read into memory. Additionally, the loading view explicitly reloads every 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb), so if retrieval never finishes the UI can loop forever showing loading.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] poll_feed calls SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) with no timeout, and the job sets sidekiq_options retry: false. A hanging or slow feed URL blocks the scheduled job indefinitely; when open raises (DNS failure, 404, malformed feed), the exception is raised in a job with retries disabled and no logging call anywhere in the diff, so feed import silently stops forever with zero operator-visible signal.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (via `open-uri`) with no explicit timeouts or exception handling. A slow/hung remote endpoint can block a Sidekiq worker thread indefinitely. Also `sidekiq_options retry: false` means transient failures (DNS, 404, malformed feed, etc.) will not be retried by Sidekiq for that execution. The finding’s claim that this will “silently stop forever” is overstated (the scheduled job would typically run again on the next recurrence and Sidekiq usually logs exceptions), but the lack of timeouts/handling in a scheduled job is a real defect exposed by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In the update path, embed.post is used without a nil check; if the post has been deleted (or post_id dangles), PostRevisor.new(nil) raises NoMethodError. PollFeed or retrieve_topic crashes with NoMethodError on nil post inside the scheduled/retry:false job, aborting the whole remaining feed items for that run, and the embed page for that URL keeps showing the loading view indefinitely because no embed state ever changes.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` when the content hash changed (app/models/topic_embed.rb, else branch). There is no guard for `embed.post` being nil (e.g., deleted post or dangling `post_id`), which would raise (at least) a `NoMethodError` inside `PostRevisor` usage. Callers like `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` and `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` don't rescue, so a single bad embed could crash the job/run and prevent subsequent items from processing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] On the update path, embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...) runs unconditionally after revisor.revise!, even when the underlying @post.save fails its validations, so the hash is advanced while the write failed. A failed post revision is recorded as done: on every subsequent poll the content_sha1 comparison shows 'no change' and the revision is never re-attempted, so the post silently stays stale forever while the pipeline reports success.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import’s update path, it calls `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)` and then `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...)`. However, the diff also changes PostRevisor to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, so with `skip_validations: true` the save explicitly bypasses validations and will not “fail its validations” as the finding claims. While `update_column` is unconditional with respect to `revise!`’s return value, the specific defect described (hash advances when validations fail) is not supported by the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When PostCreator.create returns a failed (invalid) post, the transaction commits with no TopicEmbed row created and no error raised; import returns nil silently. The retrieve_topic job completes 'successfully' while dropping the work; the user's embed iframe reloads the loading page every 30 seconds in an infinite loop with no error surfaced anywhere, because the controller will re-enqueue retrieve_topic each time and the throttle only hides it for 60s.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the `Topic.transaction` block only creates a `TopicEmbed` row when `post.present?` after `PostCreator#create` (new code: `post = creator.create; if post.present? ... TopicEmbed.create! ... end`). If `creator.create` can ever return `nil` (or otherwise fail without raising), this path will silently do nothing and return `nil` at the end of `import`. Neither `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` nor `Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute` checks the return value or raises on failure, so the job would complete without creating an embed. Separately, `EmbedController#best` enqueues `retrieve_topic` whenever `topic_id` is missing and renders `loading`, whose JS reloads every 30s—so a permanent failure to create the embed could cause repeated reload/enqueue cycles with no surfaced error (throttling only limits actual retrieval attempts for 60s). The diff doesn’t prove `PostCreator#create` can fail in this silent way, but the new code has no explicit failure handling if it does.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] retrieved_recently? commits the Redis throttle key (setnx + expire) before perform_retrieve runs, so a failed retrieve still consumes the 60-second slot. When the fetch or import fails (bad page, readability returns empty content, nil user), subsequent embed requests within 60 seconds no-op 'successfully' against the throttle, and combined with the silent nil return of fetch_http the embedding site shows the loading page indefinitely with no diagnostic.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, `retrieve` calls `retrieved_recently?` before `perform_retrieve`. `retrieved_recently?` unconditionally claims the throttle slot via `$redis.setnx` + `expire` when the key is absent, and there is no rollback if `perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http` later fails or bails early. For example, `fetch_http` can return early when `embed_by_username` doesn’t resolve to a user (`return if user.blank?`), and network/parse errors from `open(@embed_url)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` are not rescued. This means a failed attempt still suppresses further attempts for 60 seconds, which can cause repeated requests/jobs to no-op during that window while the controller renders the loading page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] fetch_http silently returns when the embed_by_username user is missing or embed_by_username is unset, with no error surfaced. A site that enables embedding but leaves embed_by_username blank gets a permanently broken embed flow: every request enqueues retrieve_topic which silently does nothing, and the loading page reloads every 30 seconds forever; nothing in the UI or logs tells the operator the setting is the cause.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` (lib/topic_retriever.rb), the user lookup is `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` and then it does `return if user.blank?`, i.e., it silently no-ops when `embed_by_username` is unset/blank (default is '' in config/site_settings.yml) or points to a nonexistent user. Nothing else in the retrieve flow checks/presents this misconfiguration: `EmbedController#best` enqueues `:retrieve_topic` when no embed exists, and `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` reloads every 30s. With a blank/missing user, the embed is never created, so the page stays in the loading/reload loop indefinitely with no surfaced error from this code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When a topic_id is found but the topic no longer exists (deleted/removed), TopicView.new raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound, producing a raw 500 on the public embed/best endpoint. A dangling TopicEmbed row (topic soft-deleted or hard-removed) turns every embed view for that URL into a server error with no recovery path — the controller never falls back to re-enqueueing retrieve_topic or rendering loading.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, the presence of a TopicEmbed row drives the "topic_id found" branch unconditionally: `topic_id = TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` (pluck) and then `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})`. There is no check that the referenced Topic still exists, and no rescue around `TopicView.new`. Since `topic_id_for_embed` does not join/verify topics, a dangling `topic_embeds.topic_id` can occur (no FK shown), which can plausibly cause an exception (e.g., RecordNotFound) and a 500 rather than falling back to enqueuing `retrieve_topic` / rendering `loading`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) raises NoMethodError when an RSS item has no content element (i.content is nil), aborting the items loop mid-iteration. One malformed item in the feed stops all subsequent feed items from being imported on every hourly run (retry: false), so the feed silently stops importing new entries with no log or error report.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If an RSS/Atom item lacks a `content` element, `i.content` can be `nil`, and calling `.scrub` on `nil` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the `rss.items.each` loop and preventing subsequent items from being imported. There is no rescue/logging here, and the job has `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so failures won’t be retried automatically.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] feed_key (the Redis key 'feed-modified:...') is defined but never read or written anywhere in the diff — the conditional fetch it was evidently built for is unimplemented. Every hourly run re-fetches and re-processes the full feed even when nothing changed, and TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve also invokes a full synchronous poll_feed on each cold embed view; large feeds multiply the outbound fetch and PostRevisor work per request with no modified-since check to short-circuit it.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `feed_key` is defined (`"feed-modified:..."`) but is never used anywhere in the diff (no Redis read/write, no If-Modified-Since logic). `poll_feed` always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all items, so each hourly run re-fetches and re-processes the whole feed regardless of changes. Additionally, lib/topic_retriever.rb `perform_retrieve` synchronously invokes `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `feed_polling_enabled?`, meaning a cold embed view can trigger a full feed fetch before falling back to HTTP import. This is a concrete performance/architecture concern grounded in the added code, not a direct correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] perform_retrieve runs Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inside the retrieve_topic worker on the embed request path. Every first-time embed view of any URL on the embeddable host triggers a full RSS/ATOM download, parse, and potential import of every feed item — one user viewing a blog post can cause dozens of topic creations, and a slow feed server delays the embed response path's worker for the full poll duration.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, `perform_retrieve` does call `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, before falling back to `fetch_http`. The `EmbedController#best` enqueues `:retrieve_topic` on first view (when no `TopicEmbed` exists), and `Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute` runs `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, so a first-time embed view can indeed cause the retrieve job to download/parse the whole feed and iterate `rss.items.each` importing each item (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`). This is a diff-grounded architectural/performance concern (potentially large side effects and long-running worker), not a strictly verifiable correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The loading view unconditionally reloads itself every 30 seconds with no retry cap or error state, combined with the retrieve flow having no failure signal back to the iframe. When retrieve_topic fails silently (nil user, failed PostCreator, throttled retry, unreachable source), the embedding site's readers get a permanently 'Loading Discussion...' iframe that hammers the Discourse embed/best endpoint every 30 seconds per visitor, indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` which unconditionally does `setTimeout(function() { document.location.reload(); }, 30000);` with no retry limit or alternate/error render. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`, but there is no mechanism in the controller/view to detect job failure or permanently missing prerequisites. The retrieve path can no-op without creating an embed (e.g., `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns if `embed_by_username` user is blank; `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`open(url)` can fail; `TopicEmbed.import` can return nil if URL invalid; throttling via `retrieved_recently?` can keep delaying retrieval). In these cases the iframe will remain in the loading page and will keep reloading `/embed/best` every 30 seconds per viewer indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import mutates the caller's contents string in place (contents << ...) before hashing and branching, so the same string passed twice gets the 'Imported from' footer appended twice. Any caller that reuses a content string across two imports (e.g. a future retry or the poll loop holding the item) silently accumulates duplicated footer HTML in the post body; also the raw caller-visible argument is mutated as a side effect.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the line `contents << "\n<hr>..."` mutates the caller-provided `contents` String in place before computing `content_sha1` and before create/update logic. If the same String object is reused across multiple calls, the footer will be appended multiple times and the content hash will change accordingly, producing duplicated footer HTML and unexpected caller-visible side effects. This in-place mutation is directly shown in the diff and is a correctness issue in the method’s behavior.
